title: One-dimensional components and completion
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring (a commutative ring with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\widehat T=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, where $\widehat A=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n$ is the maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If $T$ has an irreducible component of dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then $\widehat T$ has an irreducible component of dimension one. If $A$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring], the converse holds: a one-dimensional irreducible component of $\widehat T$ implies that $T$ has a one-dimensional irreducible component.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.6 (completion preserves dimension-one components; converse under universal catenarity)

proof.text: Put $B=\widehat A$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, put $R_{\mathfrak p}=A/\mathfrak p$ and $C_{\mathfrak p}=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}$. A quotient of a Noetherian local ring by a prime is a nonzero Noetherian local domain: ideals lift to ideals of $A$, primes are proper, and every maximal ideal lifts to $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] we identify $C_{\mathfrak p}=B/\mathfrak pB$ through the canonical compatible quotient maps. The completions $B$ and $C_{\mathfrak p}$ are Noetherian local by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Both maps $A\to B$ and $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ are faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat].

source.place: XIV, Lemma 2.1.6, general case: completion of each reduced irreducible component; the completion/quotient comparison is supplied by Stacks 00MA rather than the SGA reference printed there.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak q$ is minimal in $B$, its contraction $\mathfrak p$ is minimal in $A$: for any prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$, flat going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] produces a prime $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak r$; minimality gives $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak q$, the prime $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak pB$ is minimal in $C_{\mathfrak p}$: any smaller prime would lift to a smaller prime in $B$.

source.place: XIV, Lemma 2.1.6, last paragraph: each completed irreducible component dominates a component of the original scheme; contraction direction.

proof.text: Conversely fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ and a minimal prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $C_{\mathfrak p}$. Flat going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] for $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ shows that $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ contracts to zero: zero is a prime of the domain $R_{\mathfrak p}$, and a prime below $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ contracting to zero must equal $\overline{\mathfrak q}$. Its inverse image $\mathfrak q\subset B$ therefore contracts to $\mathfrak p$. Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ using [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. Its contraction is a prime contained in $\mathfrak p$, hence equals $\mathfrak p$; thus $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak q_0$. The minimality of $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ now forces $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q$. Consequently every component of $\operatorname{Spec}C_{\mathfrak p}$ is a component of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. Conversely Step 2 assigns every component of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ to such a $C_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: XIV, Lemma 2.1.6, last paragraph: the components of the completed reduced components are exactly the components of the completion.

proof.text: We use the following direct prime-chain interpretation throughout. For an ideal $I\subset R$, taking inverse images gives a bijection between primes of $R/I$ and primes of $R$ containing $I$, preserving inclusion and the Zariski closed sets $V(J)$; its inverse sends $\mathfrak r$ to $\mathfrak r/I$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ is homeomorphic to $V(I)$. Combine this with [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring]: components of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ have dimensions $\dim(R/\mathfrak r)$ for minimal primes $\mathfrak r$. In particular all the component identifications in Steps 2 and 3 preserve dimension.

source.place: XIV, Lemma 2.1.6, both cases: dimensions of reduced components; prime-chain form of the closed-subscheme identifications.

proof.text: For the forward implication, choose a component $V(\mathfrak p)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of dimension one. Step 4 says $\dim R_{\mathfrak p}=1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] gives $\dim C_{\mathfrak p}=1$. Choose a minimal prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $C_{\mathfrak p}$ below its maximal ideal using [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. In any local ring of dimension one no minimal prime can be its maximal ideal: if it were, every prime, being contained in that maximal ideal, would equal it, contrary to dimension one. Therefore $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is strictly below the maximal ideal. This gives a chain of length one in $C_{\mathfrak p}/\overline{\mathfrak q}$; a longer chain would lift to a chain in $C_{\mathfrak p}$, so this quotient has dimension exactly one. By Steps 3 and 4 the corresponding $V(\mathfrak q)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the required component. No catenarity hypothesis was used.

source.place: XIV, Lemma 2.1.6, integral forward case and general-case reduction.

proof.text: For the converse assume $A$ universally catenary, and choose a component $V(\mathfrak q)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$ of dimension one. Step 2 gives a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ with $\overline{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/\mathfrak pB$ minimal in $C_{\mathfrak p}$. By Step 4 this is a dimension-one component of $\operatorname{Spec}C_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-per-ratliff-formal-catenarity] to $A$: all components of this particular $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak pB)$ have the same dimension, hence all have dimension one. Every finite prime chain in $C_{\mathfrak p}$ lies above a minimal prime below its first term, by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], so it has length at most one. The chosen component supplies a length-one chain. Thus $\dim C_{\mathfrak p}=1$, and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] gives $\dim R_{\mathfrak p}=1$. Step 4 identifies $\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathfrak p}$ with the irreducible component $V(\mathfrak p)$ of $T$, proving the converse.

source.place: XIV, Lemma 2.1.6, integral converse using Theorem 1.2.2, followed by the last-paragraph component reduction.

Step 2 is correct: by going down, a minimal q of B contracts to a minimal p, and q/pB is minimal in C_p. Step 4 uses Spec(R/I) = V(I) with the 00ES node and the topological = ring dimension node. Step 5 (forward) uses 07NV for A/p; a minimal prime of a 1-dimensional local ring is not its maximal ideal, so that component has dimension exactly 1, and no catenarity is used. Step 6 (converse) applies Ratliff to A, so Spec(B/pB) is equidimensional of dimension 1, hence dim C_p = 1, hence dim A/p = 1 by 07NV. The universal-catenarity hypothesis is used exactly there.
